planting.note: Nick or soak seed before sowing directly where it will grow, since the deep taproot resists transplanting.

directions: White Pearl is a pure white-flowered selection of the vigorous perennial sweet pea, keeping the species' same climbing, tendril-clinging habit and long early-to-late-summer bloom but without the magenta and rose tones of the wild form. It is a long-cultivated named form valued for pairing cleanly with other border colors on a trellis, fence, or shrub it can scramble through. Like the species it is unscented and tolerates poor, dry soil far better than annual sweet peas, naturalizing readily once established.

planting.note: Nick or soak seed before sowing directly at the base of a support, since the deep rootstock resists transplanting.

directions: Red Pearl selects for the deepest rose-red tones found in perennial sweet pea, giving a bolder color option than the species' usual pastel pink-and-white mix while keeping the same clasping, tendril-climbing vine. It blooms over the same long early-to-late-summer window and tolerates heat, drought, and lean soil as readily as the species. Pair it with White Pearl or the species mix along a fence or large shrub for a two-tone display.

common_name: Super Spur Mayhaw (Named Western Mayhaw Selection)

planting.note: Plant bare-root or container-grown trees in late winter to early spring in moist, acidic, poorly drained soil; pair with a second mayhaw cultivar for reliable cross-pollination.

directions: Super Spur is a named western mayhaw selection grown and traded among East Texas pineywoods growers alongside sibling selections such as Lufkin and Big V, valued like them for bearing the small, tart, cherry-sized red fruit prized for traditional mayhaw jelly. As with other named mayhaw cultivars, specific published detail on its individual fruit size and ripening window is thin outside regional growing circles, so give it the same general culture as other western mayhaw selections. Plant it in full sun on seasonally wet, poorly drained, acidic ground where mayhaw thrives and most other fruit trees struggle, with a second cultivar nearby for pollination.

planting.note: Scarify seed and direct sow where plants are to grow, since lupine seedlings resent transplanting.

directions: Gallery Red is the solid deep-red color form within the compact Gallery strain, bred to bring the classic saturated Russell-type lupine palette down to a shorter, front-of-border scale that needs little staking. It carries the same dense flower spikes above palmate foliage as its Gallery Blue, Gallery Yellow, and Gallery Pink series-mates, flowering in late spring to early summer. Like other Russell-type lupines it favors cool, moist summers and declines quickly in southern heat and humidity.

planting.note: Scarify seed and direct sow where plants are to grow, since lupine seedlings resent transplanting.

directions: Gallery Blue carries a rich violet-blue self color on the same compact, well-under-two-foot spikes bred into the whole Gallery strain, giving a cooler-toned option alongside its Gallery Red and Gallery Yellow series-mates. The dense, uncrowded habit suits patio containers and small cottage borders where taller Russell-type lupines would need staking. It shares the strain's preference for cool, moist summers and a permanent planting site, since the taproot resents disturbance once established.

planting.note: Scarify seed and direct sow where plants are to grow, since lupine seedlings resent transplanting.

directions: Gallery Yellow brings a clear golden self color to the compact Gallery strain, standing out against the more common blue and red tones of its Gallery series-mates in a mixed planting. Dense flower spikes form on the same short, sturdy, front-of-border scale the whole strain was bred for, needing no staking even in open sites. Start seed where it is to grow and expect the best performance in regions with cool summers, since heat and humidity shorten bloom and vigor.

planting.note: Scarify seed and direct sow where plants are to grow, since lupine seedlings resent transplanting.

directions: Gallery Pink offers a softer rose-pink self color within the compact Gallery strain, a gentler complement to the saturated Gallery Red and Gallery Blue selections sold alongside it. It keeps the strain's short, dense, well-branched habit, flowering heavily in late spring without the staking taller Russell-type lupines need. Give it a permanent spot in cool-summer gardens, since the deep taproot dislikes transplanting and performance fades quickly in hot, humid summers.

common_name: Lucky Star Deep Pink Pentas (Compact Texas Superstar Star-Cluster Pentas)

planting.note: Transplant after soil has warmed following the last frost; Deep Pink is one of the saturated color options in the dwarf Lucky Star seed series.

directions: Lucky Star Deep Pink carries rich magenta-pink star-shaped flower clusters on the same tight, uniform dwarf habit bred into the whole Lucky Star series, staying compact through a full Gulf South summer without stretching. It flowers continuously from late spring to frost and draws steady butterfly and hummingbird traffic in mass beds and containers. Grow in full sun in fertile, well-drained soil with regular water while establishing, then taper off once plants fill in.

common_name: Lucky Star Violet Pentas (Compact Texas Superstar Star-Cluster Pentas)

planting.note: Transplant after soil has warmed following the last frost; Violet is one of the cooler-toned colors in the dwarf Lucky Star seed series.

directions: Lucky Star Violet bears clusters of rich purple-violet star-shaped flowers on the series' signature tight, dwarf mound, offering a deeper jewel tone alongside its Lavender and Deep Pink series-mates. Plants hold their compact shape in mass plantings and containers through heavy summer heat and humidity without flopping. Provide full sun and fertile, well-drained soil, watering regularly during establishment for the heaviest, longest-lasting bloom from late spring into fall.

common_name: Lucky Star Lipstick Pentas (Compact Texas Superstar Star-Cluster Pentas)

planting.note: Transplant after soil has warmed following the last frost; Lipstick is a bright coral-red color option in the dwarf Lucky Star seed series.

directions: Lucky Star Lipstick opens vivid coral-red star clusters on the series' tidy, uniform dwarf mound, a brighter, warmer tone than the true Dark Red selection in the same line. It holds its compact habit and continuous bloom through Gulf Coast summer heat, drawing butterflies and hummingbirds from late spring through the first frost. Grow in full sun in fertile, well-drained soil with regular moisture while establishing, then feed lightly through the season to keep clusters coming.

common_name: Lucky Star White Improved Pentas (Compact Texas Superstar Star-Cluster Pentas)

planting.note: Transplant after soil has warmed following the last frost; White Improved is a refined, cleaner-flowering white selection within the dwarf Lucky Star seed series.

directions: Lucky Star White Improved produces crisp white star-shaped flower clusters on the series' compact, tidy mound, selected as an improvement over earlier white Lucky Star stock for cleaner color and more uniform flowering. Its pale blooms show especially well at dusk and against darker companion foliage while still drawing butterflies and hummingbirds through the day. Grow in full sun in fertile, well-drained soil, watering consistently through establishment and feeding lightly for continuous bloom into fall.
